text: {"dataset_name":"adult_income","model_family":"tree","schema_generator":"claude-sonnet-4.6","schema_version":"1.0","features":[{"name":"high_education_flag","type":"formula","description":"Binary indicator for college-level or higher education (education_num >= 13 corresponds to Bachelors or above)","value_range":[0,1],"feature_family":"education","expected_model_benefit":"Direct split on high-education threshold strongly associated with income level","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where(education_num >= 13, 1, 0)"},{"name":"capital_net","type":"formula","description":"Net capital activity: capital_gain minus capital_loss, capturing overall investment income signal","value_range":[-4356,99999],"feature_family":"capital","expected_model_benefit":"Single feature combining two sparse capital signals; large positive values strongly indicate higher income","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"capital_gain - capital_loss"},{"name":"capital_active_flag","type":"formula","description":"Binary indicator that the person has any capital activity (gain or loss > 0)","value_range":[0,1],"feature_family":"capital","expected_model_benefit":"Separates people with investment activity from those without; investment activity correlates with wealth","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where((capital_gain > 0) | (capital_loss > 0), 1, 0)"},{"name":"log1p_capital_gain","type":"formula","description":"Log-transformed capital gain to compress extreme outliers while preserving ordering","value_range":[0,11.51],"feature_family":"capital","expected_model_benefit":"Reduces skew in capital_gain; tree splits on compressed scale are more informative across the distribution","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.log1p(capital_gain)"},{"name":"married_flag","type":"formula","description":"Binary indicator for married-with-spouse status (marital_status == 2 typically encodes Married-civ-spouse)","value_range":[0,1],"feature_family":"marital","expected_model_benefit":"Married individuals have substantially different income distributions; direct boolean split is highly effective for trees","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where(marital_status == 2, 1, 0)"},{"name":"age_bucket","type":"formula","description":"Ordinal age bucket: 0=young(17-25), 1=early-career(26-35), 2=mid-career(36-50), 3=senior(51-65), 4=retirement(66+)","value_range":[0,4],"feature_family":"age","expected_model_benefit":"Ordinal bucketing captures nonlinear age-income relationship better than raw age for tree splits","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where(age <= 25, 0, np.where(age <= 35, 1, np.where(age <= 50, 2, np.where(age <= 65, 3, 4))))"},{"name":"hours_fulltime_flag","type":"formula","description":"Binary indicator for full-time or overtime work (hours_per_week >= 40)","value_range":[0,1],"feature_family":"work_intensity","expected_model_benefit":"Full-time workers have higher income probability; clean boolean split for tree models","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where(hours_per_week >= 40, 1, 0)"},{"name":"hours_deviation_from_40","type":"formula","description":"Absolute deviation of hours_per_week from standard 40-hour work week","value_range":[0,59],"feature_family":"work_intensity","expected_model_benefit":"Captures both under- and over-work relative to standard; extreme deviations in either direction carry income signal","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.abs(hours_per_week - 40)"},{"name":"education_hours_interaction","type":"formula","description":"Product of education_num and hours_per_week, capturing combined human capital and effort signal","value_range":[1,1584],"feature_family":"interaction","expected_model_benefit":"Nonlinear interaction between education and work hours; high values indicate both educated and hardworking individuals","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"education_num * hours_per_week"},{"name":"private_sector_flag","type":"formula","description":"Binary indicator for private-sector employment (workclass == 4 typically encodes Private)","value_range":[0,1],"feature_family":"employment","expected_model_benefit":"Private sector workers have different income distributions than government or self-employed; useful split point","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"np.where(workclass == 4, 1, 0)"},{"name":"age_education_score","type":"formula","description":"Combined score of age and education_num normalized: age divided by 90 plus education_num divided by 16, capturing life-stage human capital","value_range":[0.25,2.0],"feature_family":"interaction","expected_model_benefit":"Combines career stage and education into a single continuous score; useful for trees to find high-human-capital individuals","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true,"formula":"(age / 90.0) + (education_num / 16.0)"},{"name":"high_skill_occupation","type":"judgment","description":"Semantic score from 0 to 3 indicating occupation skill level: 0=low-skill/service/manual (occupation in 0-3,7-9), 1=mid-skill clerical/sales (occupation in 4-6), 2=high-skill technical/managerial (occupation in 10-12), 3=top professional/executive (occupation == 13)","value_range":[0,3],"feature_family":"occupation","expected_model_benefit":"Ordinal skill grouping of occupation codes enables tree to split on meaningful skill tiers rather than arbitrary numeric codes","leakage_risk":"low","uses_only_row_values":true}]}
